Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! Bangladeshi fielders are in a huddle and then they spread out on the field. Tom Blundell and Rachin Ravindra to open the innings. Mahedi Hasan to start with the ball.

The bowling from New Zealand was dominated by Rachin Ravindra. The spinner took 3 wickets and gave just 22 runs. Cole McConchie and Ajaz Patel also took a wicket each and were quite good. It looked like they would restrict Bangladesh to a par score but Hamish Bennett and Doug Bracewell were put under the pump in the last two overs. But that is in the past and it is now time for the Kiwi batters to chase this down. Will they be able to do so? We will find out. Do not go anywhere as the chase comes our way shortly.

Bangladesh had a good start at the top. They did not get off to a flier but Mohammad Naim and Liton Das started with a 50-run stand and set the tone. There was a mini-collapse as Mushfiqur Rahim and Shakib Al Hasan did not contribute much. But Mahmudullah and Nurul Hasan hit some lusty blows in the death overs to get them to 141.
A really good batting show by Bangladesh. A score of 140 on this track is very competitive and given their bowling attack, the hosts would be confident of defending this.

OUT! TAKEN! That is a superb take! A wicket to end the innings! Shorter again and on middle. Hasan pulls, this goes more off the top edge towards deep mid-wicket. Will Young runs in, dives forward and takes a brilliant catch. Still, quite a decent last over for Bangladesh. BANGLADESH END WITH 141!
Commentary.Howout: c Will Young b Hamish Bennett

Commentary.Commentary: Another two! Shorter again, Hasan pulls, not off the middle but it lands safe in the mid-wicket region. Easy two.
FOUR! Welcome one! Really clever shot! Uses the depth of the crease here! Shorter and on middle, Hasan gets down on one knee and pulls it behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
A low full toss, it is dragged wide of the fielder at deep mid-wicket for two more. The last two overs are proving to be really good.
Angled into the pads, Mahmudullah looks to flick but misses. It hits the pad and goes towards the leg side for one. Leg bye.
Two! Brilliant running! On the pads, this is worked through square leg for two.
A single to end but a huge over! Outside off, this is hit through covers for one.
Two more! Very well fielded! Mahmudullah plays the paddle scoop, it is running towards the fine leg fence. The fielder there runs to his right, slides and saves two.

FOUR! Just over! Shorter and on middle, Mahmudullah pulls, it goes towards deep mid-wicket. The fielder there is quite inside, probably because it is the bigger area. It goes over him and for a boundary. Not sure why he needs to be standing so inside given that it is the penultimate over.
FOUR! Off the outside edge! Mahmudullah comes down the track, this is bowled full and wide outside off, Mahmudullah slashes, it goes off the outside edge over short third man for a boundary.
Another single! On off, this is pulled down to long on.
Well bowled! Shorter and around off, Mahmudullah looks to guide it down to third man, this goes off the glove towards short third man for one.
Length ball, on off. Pushed to long on. There is a direct hit at the bowler's end and the ball is deflected. The batters steal another run.
Length ball, on off. Pushed to covers for one.

NOT OUT! Full ball, on off. Hasan goes for the paddle and it looks like he has been hit on the pads. The appeal for LBW is turned down. The ball goes towards cover and the batters cross over. New Zealand take the review but the replay shows that the ball has hit the bat.
Review time. New Zealand have reviewed this for LBW. Well, well, the ball has hit the bat.
Length ball, on leg. Mahmudullah taps it to the leg side for one.
Full ball, on the pads. Worked away to square leg for one.
Shorter ball, outside off. Pulled away to deep mid-wicket for one.

BEATEN! That is a beauty again! This lands around middle and then spins away. Hasan goes back to defend but is beaten. What an over from Patel. Outstanding. End of his spell too and he too has been magical.
Angled into the pads, this is worked on the leg side for one.
Another dot! On off, Mahmudullah guides it to point.
BEAUTY! This is slower, it lands around off and spins away. Mahmudullah looks to defend but is beaten.

OUT! TAKEN! Another one bites the dust! Bangladesh losing their way now! Afif Hossain comes down the track, gets a little too close to the pitch of the ball. He lofts it towards long on. It goes off the bottom and it is a simple catch for Colin de Grandhomme. Nurul Hasan walks out to bat.
Commentary.Howout: c Colin de Grandhomme b Ajaz Patel

Commentary.Commentary: Two more! Shorter and outside off, Hossain cuts it through point. Two taken.

Just short! Afif gets lucky! This is on middle, Afif Hossain straightaway looks to play the slog sweep, due to the extra bounce, it goes off the splice but lands safe in the mid-wicket region. One taken. End of a brilliant spell by Rachin Ravindra.
Who will bat now? Afif Hossain it is.

OUT! TAKEN! Naim now has to walk back! Timely wicket as Naim was well set! He had to go for it, he was striking at below 100. This is on middle, Naim looks to go over long on, the length was way too full, he ends up hitting it straight to the fielder there. Tom Blundell takes it with ease. Can the Kiwis now keep the hosts under 150?
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Blundell b Rachin Ravindra

Commentary.Commentary: Shorter yet again and on middle, Naim works it to mid-wicket. Dots are gold at this stage.
Flatter and on the pads again, it is nudged on the leg side for one more.
Another fumble and another run! On middle, this is worked towards mid-wicket for one.
Fires it on the pads, this is worked towards square leg for one.
A single to end! 11 from the over then! A full toss outside off, Mahmudullah hits it through covers for one.
FOUR! Lovely placement and the 100 is up! Mahmudullah comes down the track and also makes room, he smashes it through covers for the second boundary in the over.
Mahmudullah misses out! Shorter and outside off, this is guided but to point.
WIDE! Mahmudullah looks to play the paddle scoop, this is banged short though. Goes well over the batter's head. Wided.
Just inside the tramline! Sees Mahmudullah come down the track and bowls it wide outside off. Mahmudullah leaves it. Not wided.
FOUR! That is a lovely stroke! Pace on the ball and it is put away! Outside off, Mahmudullah guides it through point, this one races away to the fence.
Drop and run! Length and on middle, cramping the batter for room. Naim pushes it towards cover and takes one.

This one stays low! On off, Mahmudullah looks to defend but this one does not bounce a lot. It goes off the underedge towards short third man. So a brilliant comeback after going for a boundary on the first ball.
Another run! Shorter and on middle, Naim pulls but too close to long on. Only one.
On middle, this is worked through square leg for one.
On the stumps again, defended.
Shorter and outside off, this is guided to point.

FOUR! Chance goes abegging! So unlike the Kiwis again! Tom Blundell it is! This is tossed up on off, Mahmudullah lofts it to the left of long off. Blundell there runs to his left and also runs in. He then realizes it is going over him, leaps and sticks a hand out, it goes over him and for a one-bounce boundary. Had he ran along the fence, would have been an easy catch. Big miss.
Just the three from the over then! Shorter and fires it on middle, Naim guides it late to point. There is an appeal from Latham, he probably felt it hit the pad first.
Another single! Outside off, Mahmudullah pushes it through covers for one more.
Outside off, this is pushed through covers for one.
Shorter and outside off, Mahmudullah looks to cut, he gets an under edge which goes between the legs of the keeper and behind him for one.
Outside off, this is pushed to covers.
On middle, Mahmudullah plays it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Up and over! Fuller and outside off, this is lofted over covers for a boundary. Two boundaries to end. Spoils the over.
FOUR! EDGY! Naim won't care! Frustration though for New Zealand! Fuller and outside off, Naim goes after it, it goes off the outside edge, just wide of Latham and down to the third man fence.
Really full and on middle, this is jammed down to mid on for one.
Another one! Shorter and outside off, this is guided through point for one.
Uppish but safe! On middle, Mahmudullah works it uppishly wide of mid-wicket for one.
Fuller and on middle, Naim works it to mid-wicket.

OUT! TAKEN IN THE END! That is a really good catch! This is tossed up on off, it is lofted down toward the long off area. Ben Sears runs in and seems to have taken it cleanly. The umpires take it upstairs and replays show that it did pop out but it bounced off his thigh as he comes in sliding and lobbed up to him nicely. He ends up taking it on the second attempt. Shakib played with a lot of intent but that shot was not needed with this already being a good over.
Commentary.Howout: c Ben Sears b Cole McConchie

Commentary.Commentary: Has that been taken? It is referred, seems a clean catch. The SOFT SIGNAL IS OUT!
FOUR! Put away! This is not a good over for the hosts, especially after Rachin Ravindra's previous over. Shorter and outside off, this is slapped through covers for a boundary.
Another single! Naim comes down the track and works it down to long on for one.
Now takes one as this is cut through point.
FOUR! Smashed! Shakib has come out with intent here! He skips down the track and slams it straight back over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Two! On the pads, Shakib works it fine and takes two!
Shakib is off the mark! Comes down the track and works it through square leg for one.
Uppish but short! Shakib comes down the track and looks to flick, he is early in closing the face of his bat. It goes off the leading edge back to the bowler.
Shakib Al Hasan walks out to bat! He will be facing the hat-trick ball.

OUT! RAHIM INDEED IS OUT OF HIS CREASE! Rahim bags a first-baller! New Zealand have two in two and are right back into this one now. This is a beauty of a delivery. This lands on off and then spins away. Rahim lunges to defend but then is beaten. Latham whips the bails off and is celebrating. They take it upstairs. Replays show that Rahim did drag his back foot outside the crease but then made no effort to take it back in.
Commentary.Howout: st Tom Latham b Rachin Ravindra

Commentary.Commentary: Have New Zealand got another one? A stumping appeal is referred. Latham is very confident.
Mushfiqur Rahim walks out to bat!

OUT! TIMBER! Quite a strange dismissal that one! Yes, the shot selection was not right but wondering how that went back onto the stumps. Rachin Ravindra gets his revenge! This lands around off, slightly shorter, spins away. Das looks to work it on the leg side very gently, it goes off the inside edge and then onto the stumps. It actually bounced just ahead of his legs and then turned back towards the stumps. Much-needed wicket for the Kiwis.
Slightly quicker this time and on off. Das pushes it to covers.
SIX! Nailed that one! Over the fence! On middle, Das shuffles across and plays the slog sweep, it goes well over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie. Welcome biggie.
Another single! On off, this is pushed through covers for one more.
On middle, this is pushed down to long on for one.
Shorter and well wide outside off, it is slapped through covers for one.
WIDE! Fires it outside off, he maybe felt the batter is going to charge at him. Das leaves it alone.
Darts it on off, Das guides it to point.
Fuller and outside off, this is slapped down to long off for one.
Another misfield! Shorter and outside off, Das pushes it through covers, it goes through the fielder for one. This is so not like New Zealand. They are usually exceptional in the field.
Another single to end! Outside off, this is pushed through covers for one. A good start by Rachin Ravindra.
Naim makes room and this is shorter and outside off, it is slapped through covers for one.
Another single as this is pushed down to long on.
A single! Shorter and on middle, Naim works it through square leg for one.
How has that missed the off pole? The extra bounce saves Naim! This is tossed up on off, Naim looks to play the slog sweep but misses. It goes just over the off pole.
Tosses it up on off, it is pushed through covers for one.
Rachin Ravindra is on now!
A dot to end! Slightly shorter again and outside off, it is cut to point.
Two more! This time to the left of the fielder at sweeper cover. Outside off, this is slapped through point for two.
Misfield and one! On off, Das walks across and works it towards mid-wicket, the fielder dives over the ball. A single.
Naim now comes down the track and then eases it down to long off for one.
Really good shot! This is very full again and outside off, it is pushed through covers for two.
Tosses it up on off, fuller, it is pushed to covers.

Just a single from it in the end! Could have been hit away for a boundary! It is a very short and very slow ball. Naim first looks to leave it but then decides to tap it towards short fine leg for one. Not sure why he did not go hard at that one. A sedate start by Bangladesh but they have not lost a wicket. They are 36 for 0 after the first 6.
Brilliant fielding! Shorter and outside off, Naim looks to guide it past point who is quite close. The fielder dives to his right and stops it.
Two more! On the pads, Naim works it through backward square leg. The short fine leg fielder runs to his right, he dives early and hence, gets only fingertips to it. Two taken.
Now follows the boundary with a single as this is nudged around the corner.

TOP EDGE AND FOUR! Fortunate boundary but Das won't care! Fuller and around off, Das looks to heave it over the leg side. This flies off the outside edge, over short third man for a boundary. Welcome boundary.
Another quick run! On middle, this is worked to mid on for a single.
A couple to end! Not a bad start from Doug! Six from his first. Das walks right across and this is bowled shorter and on middle, it is pulled towards deep square leg for two.
In the air... safe! A short one, it hurries onto the batter. Naim looks to pull, it goes off the splice and just over mid-wicket for one. A good over so far but can Bracewell end it well?
Really well fielded! Fuller and on middle, Naim drives it crisply but back to the bowler who gets down quickly and stops it.
Just another one! Slightly shorter and outside off, Das guides it to short third man and gets to the other end.
Shorter and on middle, this is worked on the leg side for one.
Really good timing but does not find the gap! Fuller and on middle, Das works it towards mid on where the fielder dives to his right and stops it. A single.
Doug Bracewell is on now!
FOUR! The last ball spoils the over somewhat! This is full and outside off, right in the slot. Naim drives it through covers and this one races away to the fence.

Another slower short ball, this lands and comes ever so slowly. Das is way too early in the pull, he misses, it hits his body and rolls on the off side for one. No signal from the umpire so there might be an under edge.
Quick run! Rotation of strike is very important on such wickets! On off, this is pushed to mid off for a single.
Once again the slowness of the wicket is very evident there! A slower short one, Naim is early into the pull, it goes off the under edge to the keeper.
Yet another dot! On off, Naim pushes it nicely but to covers.
A slower one, full and outside off. Naim looks to drive but due to the slowness, it goes off the inner half back to the bowler.
Outside off, this is guided to point. A good comeback then by Patel after going for 9 in the first three balls.
Flatter and on middle, Das keeps it out.
Good stop! This is tossed up again, this lands and then turns away. Das looks to go over covers, it goes off the outer half towards short third man who dives to his left and stops it.
FOUR MORE! This one is off the back foot! Shorter and outside off, Das stays back and slaps it through covers for the second boundary in the over. Really good over so far. 9 from it.
FOUR! Lovely shot! Patel floats it up on off, this is nice and full outside off, Das leans into it and lofts it over covers for a boundary.
The slog sweep is out, Naim hits it through mid-wicket, there is a fielder in the deep so only one.
A tidy start from Cole too! On off, extra bounce. Das blocks it by taking a hand off the handle.

EDGY RUNS! No slip in place and two is taken! On off, this one goes on with the arm. Das looks to flick, it goes off the leading edge through the vacant first slip region for two. Das is off the mark.
A huge appeal but turned down! Das walks right across the stumps. This lands outside off, he tries to sweep but misses. An appeal but turned down. Impact is outside off.

DROPPED! That is a sitter! Colin de Grandhomme can't believe he has dropped that! It is short and on middle, Das looks to pull but it goes more off the splice and towards square leg. Colin de Grandhomme spills it. This could prove costly. Das is a very dangerous batter.
Good running! Shorter and on off, Naim guides it towards point, it is to his right and they take a quick run.
Shorter and outside off, this is guided to point.
Cole McConchie to bowl from the other end!
Another dot to end so a good start by Ajaz! On middle yet again, Das pushes it to covers.
Flatter and on middle, Das defends it out.
Slower through the air and outside off, left alone. Good turn for Patel.
Another single as Naim plays another sweep through square leg for one.
Flatter and on middle, this one turns back in. Naim looks to flick but misses to get hit high on the pads.

Two! Naim is underway! He goes for the slog sweep straight away, this lands on middle, he connects well, it goes towards deep square leg. The fielder in the deep runs to his left, slides and saves two for his side. Bangladesh and Naim are underway!
We are all set for the action to begin! The Bangladesh openers, Liton Das and Mohammad Naim walk out to the centre. Ajaz Patel to bowl. Here we go...

Tom Latham says they wanted to bat first too but they are now bowling first and he hopes they can get some early wickets. States the way they came out with the ball was very good, it was small target and they bowled decently. He hopes they can do better here and get the important wickets. Also says the guys reflected on what they could have done better and they are looking forward to this game. Informs they have two changes, Hamish Bennett and Ben Sears come in for Blair Tickner and Jacob Duffy.

Mahmudullah says they need to have a good start, he expects the wicket to remain the same. Adds it is always important to get early wickets so that you can put the opposition under pressure and it is important to start well and put some runs on the board. Mentions the wicket looks similar and they need to get to something aroun 130 or 140 and that will be a challenging score. Ends by saying the spinners have bowled very well and they have a good bowling unit.

PITCH REPORT - Athar Ali Khan says this is pitch number 3 but it looks similar to the surface on which they played the first game. States it will be good for the spinners. Adds the Bangladesh seamers have done well too with their cutters. Mentions it is not a high-scoring ground and you need to rotate strike and wait for the loose balls.

NEW ZEALAND (PLAYING XI) - Tom Blundell, Rachin Ravindra, Will Young, Colin de Grandhomme, Tom Latham (WK/C), Henry Nicholls, Cole McConchie, Doug Bracewell, Ajaz Patel, Hamish Bennett (IN FOR Blair Tickner), Ben Sears (IN FOR Jacob Duffy).

BANGLADESH (UNCHANGED PLAYING XI) - Mohammad Naim, Liton Das, Shakib Al Hasan, Mushfiqur Rahim, Mahmudullah (C), Afif Hossain, Nurul Hasan (WK), Mahedi Hasan, Mohammad Saifuddin, Mustafizur Rahman, Nasum Ahmed.
TOSS - Bangladesh have won the toss and have ELECTED TO BAT!

A loss here for the visitors will make it very difficult for them to make a comeback into the series and a win for Bangladesh will see them inch closer of recording yet another series win on home soil. A very important clash awaits. Stay tuned for the toss in a bit.

For Bangladesh, they are just growing in confidence at the moment. They recorded their first ever series win over Australia some time back and now their first ever win in T20Is over the Kiwis. Yes, this is not a full-strength New Zealand side but take nothing away from the brand of cricket the hosts are playing. Also, winning is a habit and that is one habit they would love to develop heading into the T20 World Cup.

Now when we say better, you'll might be wondering, surely, New Zealand can't do worse, surely they would better their performance! However, the wicket here keeps getting tough, we saw that in the Australia series, that scores kept going down in each game as the wicket started to take more and more turn. Most of the New Zealand batters are quite inexperienced, these are alien-like conditions for them so one can't count out them being bundled out for another very low score.

It was Australia who were embarrassed by Bangladesh some time ago and now the Kiwis went down in quite a humiliating manner. The sides from Down Under have found out that batting is not going to be easy the hard way. Australia failed to cross the 130-run mark in their 5-match T20I series with their lowest score being 62. The New Zealand side were bundled out for 2 lesser than what was Australia's lowest in the former's first game, 60 to be precise. They were decimated by the Bangladeshi spinners. Will we see a better outing for them with the bat this time? We will find out. Welcome to the coverage.
